items.headline: Stocks ended Thursday's sell-off at their lowest since spring; I couldn't find Friday's close
items.note: On Thursday the S&P 500 closed at 7,175.83, the Nasdaq at 23,879.20 and the Dow at 49,097.06, each down more than 2% as worries grew that the AI boom is fading. Reports say the S&P 500 had lost ground six days running and sat at its lowest level since April.

items.headline: Wednesday's drop: Dow lost 561 points, S&P 500 slipped 0.23%
items.note: The Dow fell 561.25 points to 50,198.17 and the S&P 500 fell 16.90 points to 7,323.63 on Nov. 18. Read next to Thursday, it shows the slide picking up speed.

items.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq: priced at $83, closes day one at $97.17
items.note: The stock closed up about 17% from the IPO price after a first-day high near $115, and it faded through the day. Trading volume was heavy even as AI stocks sold off.

items.headline: Anthropic: up to 315M existing shares could be sold from day one; Q3 swung to an operating loss
items.note: Search summaries say a Nov. 17 filing amendment allowed those sales, and that operating profit of $974M in Q2 became a $567M operating loss in Q3. I didn't confirm these on the original pages. Share supply and profitability are what analysts are watching.

items.headline: Nvidia: Bessent's 10-day deadline for the board lands around Nov. 25
items.note: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12 and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Treasury Secretary Bessent wants an outside successor and answers on China chip sales. Export-control and governance news now moves AI chip stocks.

items.headline: Nvidia board reportedly floated Arm CEO Rene Haas; big investors want a slow search
items.note: The FT reportedly said Haas was floated. Investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker asked for a deliberate process that leaves room for Huang's return. Both points come from a search summary, not a page I read.

items.headline: Fed meets Dec. 8–9 with a quarter-point hike widely expected
items.note: The Fed hiked in September and held Oct. 28 on a 10-2 vote, with two officials wanting another hike; the range is 3.75%–4.00%. After October payrolls rose 165,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, markets put a December hike near 77% (as of Nov. 6, so odds may have moved). The November jobs report is due Dec. 4.

items.headline: Tech layoffs pass 142,000 this year, yet data scientist postings are rising
items.note: Layoffs.fyi counted more than 142,000 tech layoffs as of Nov. 11. The same source says CompTIA saw double-digit posting gains for data scientists in October, though entry-level hiring stays weak, so internship applications should go out early.

learn.explain: Operating profit is what a company earns from its core business after paying the costs of running it, such as salaries, computing and marketing, but before interest and taxes. If a company sells $100 of services and spends $80 running the business, its operating profit is $20. Anthropic's reported swing from a $974M operating profit in Q2 to a $567M operating loss in Q3 (per search summaries) shows how fast this number can move when spending jumps. Investors look at it because it shows whether the core business makes money, without one-off items.
learn.try: Look up the operating margin (operating profit divided by revenue) of a company you use, like Apple or Nvidia.
